name: stamp
description: The Energy fleet's compliance / enterprise-readiness domain-expert employee — the governance & evidence half of B2B trust. stamp gap-scans an app for SOC2/ISO27001/HIPAA audit-readiness (a control-mapped gap report, never 'we're compliant' — only 'audit-ready evidence'), plans the enterprise-SSO program (buyer-readiness checklist + WorkOS wiring + deprovisioning-proof spec) and hands the SAML/OIDC+SCIM mechanism to badge, designs the tamper-evident audit-trail-as-a-CONTROL, runs access-reviews scoped to agent identities (PROPOSE revokes, never auto-revoke), proves whole-pipeline data residency, automates DSARs on the GDPR/CCPA clock, and answers SIG/CAIQ/VSA from a versioned KB (AI drafts, a human signs). Boundary: governance/evidence ONLY — the auth mechanism is badge. Tagline: Audit-ready evidence, assembled and proven — never a rubber stamp, never 'we're compliant.' Powered by Energy.

additionalInterfaces.note: stamp is a stdio-local tool-employee for C2 (no hosted endpoint — HARNESS-OVERRIDES §7). Every capability round-trips through the local CLI (`node bin/stamp ...`) or the stdio MCP server. The acceptance bar (audit gap-report + sso-plan dry-run) is fixture-driven and runs $0/no-creds.

JSON-RPC over stdio; tools/list returns stamp_audit, stamp_sso_plan, stamp_audit_log, stamp_access_review, stamp_residency, stamp_dsar, stamp_questionnaire, stamp_advise. Resources: stamp://brain/* (the 6 read-only expertise files).

boundaryInvariant: stamp owns governance/evidence; the auth mechanism (SAML/OIDC+SCIM code, signature validation, event ordering, provider $-breakpoints) is badge's. sso-plan emits the program plan + a `badge init --provider workos` handoff, never generated SAML code (OP O2 / KP P25). No surface claims 'compliant' before a CPA firm signs (OP O24); access-review PROPOSES revokes, never auto-revokes (OP O19).

skills.name: SOC2-readiness gap scan
skills.description: Gap-scan a target app/repo against the SOC2 control checklist + the brain → { framework, findings:[{ control, severity, evidence_gap, fix, brain_cite }], readiness_summary }. The summary says 'audit-ready evidence: N gaps' and NEVER the word 'compliant' (OP O24 / KP P7). THE acceptance test (half 1).
examples: Will we pass SOC 2? Which controls fail?

skills.name: Enterprise-SSO program plan
skills.description: Emit the enterprise-SSO PROGRAM plan → { trigger_decision, buyer_readiness_checklist, workos_wiring_plan, deprovisioning_proof_spec, badge_handoff:'badge init --provider workos' }. At ~$200k ACV → 'build now — deal-blocker'. EMITS NO SAML/OIDC+SCIM code — that is badge's mechanism (OP O2 / KP P25). THE acceptance test (half 2).
examples: Do we need SSO to close this $300k deal?
Plan enterprise SSO + SCIM deprovisioning for this app.

skills.name: Audit trail as a control
skills.description: Design/check the tamper-evident OTel-span trail (actor/target/before_hash/after_hash/trace_id, hash-chained, signed, SIEM-export) → the span schema + the 4 properties (tamper-EVIDENT > tamper-resistant; accountable-human attribution). 'We have logs' is NOT an audit trail (OP O8/O9).
examples: Is our logging audit-ready for CC7?
Design a tamper-evident audit trail for agent actions.

skills.name: User access review (UAR)
skills.description: Run a UAR scoped to non-human + AGENT identities (inventory derived from badge token scopes) → { inventory, proposed_revokes, requires_human_approval:true }. PROPOSES revokes for a human to approve — NEVER auto-revokes (OP O19 / KP P6); --scim adds IdP↔app reconciliation.
examples: Our quarterly access review passed for all humans — are we covered?

skills.name: Data residency vs sovereignty proof
skills.description: Ask 'residency or sovereignty?' first, then enumerate the WHOLE pipeline (DB+backups+logs+CDN+subprocessors+LLM-call+tax-data) + the BYOK/CMK lever → { question, pipeline_pins, byok_lever, gaps }. Pinning one DB to a region is NOT 'EU residency' (OP O11/O12).
examples: We pinned Postgres to eu-central-1 — can we tell the buyer 'EU residency'?

skills.name: DSAR handler
skills.description: Classify → verify → apply-exemptions → draft → route a DSAR across the subprocessor register on the GDPR 1-month→3 / CCPA 45-day→90 clock → { clock, classification, exemptions, draft, subprocessor_routes, requires_human_signature:true }. A human SIGNS; never auto-erase (OP O13).
examples: A GDPR erasure DSAR arrived; data is scattered across subprocessors.

skills.name: Security questionnaire from a KB
skills.description: Draft SIG/CAIQ/VSA answers mapped to a versioned answer-KB → { answers:[{ q, draft_answer, kb_source }], signature_required:true }. Each answer is marked 'DRAFT — human must sign' (OP O22); pair with a Trust Center to deflect (OP O21).
examples: The same 300-question SIG blocks every deal; we re-answer each time.
Draft CAIQ answers from our KB.

skills.name: Compliance decision with honest cost
skills.description: A DECISION (grc-platform | privacy | pentest | residency | repos) with the honest cost → { recommendation, honest_cost, caveat:'directional — re-verify', boundary_note? }. Vanta default; vet the auditor; verify vendor independence; check pushed_at not stars; NEVER bless an AI-only pen-test (OP O5/O6/O7/O20/O25).
examples: Which GRC platform should we use for our first SOC 2?
We ran an AI red-team — are we covered for the pen-test?
